Interpretation: Model Comparison¶

  • HistGradientBoosting has the strongest overall balance (highest macro-F1).
  • Gradient Boosting achieves the highest recall for class 2 (2+ admissions), which is useful for high-risk targeting.
  • Random Forest shows high accuracy but poor balanced accuracy and weak minority recall, indicating majority-class bias.

7. Confusion Matrices Purpose: visualize error patterns for the baseline model and the model with the highest recall for class 2.

In [8]:
# Purpose: This notebook compares model performance, interprets the final model, and generates the primary diagnostic outputs used in the report. | code block 8.
baseline_name = "HistGradientBoosting"
best_recall2_name = comparison.sort_values("Recall_2", ascending=False).iloc[0]["Model"]

names = [baseline_name]
if best_recall2_name != baseline_name:
    names.append(best_recall2_name)

print("Best by Recall_2:", best_recall2_name)

for name in names:
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, preds[name], labels=[0, 1, 2])
    disp = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(confusion_matrix=cm, display_labels=[0, 1, 2])
    disp.plot(cmap="Blues", values_format="d")
    plt.title(f"Confusion Matrix: {name}")
    plt.show()

Best by Recall_2: Gradient Boosting

Interpretation: Confusion Matrix¶

  • Most errors are between adjacent classes (0 vs 1 or 1 vs 2), not extreme jumps.
  • The model captures some high-risk cases but also misses many and flags some non high-risk individuals.

8. High-Risk Precision-Recall Curves Purpose: examine precision-recall tradeoffs for predicting the high-risk class (2+ admissions).

In [9]:
# Purpose: This notebook compares model performance, interprets the final model, and generates the primary diagnostic outputs used in the report. | code block 9.
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))

names = [baseline_name]
if best_recall2_name != baseline_name:
    names.append(best_recall2_name)

for name in names:
    model = trained[name]
    class_index = list(model.classes_).index(2)
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_test_bin, probas[name][:, class_index])
    plt.plot(recall, precision, label=name)

plt.xlabel("Recall")
plt.ylabel("Precision")
plt.title("PR Curve for High-Risk Class (2+ Admissions)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()

Interpretation: PR Curve¶

  • Precision falls as recall increases because class 2 is rare.
  • Use the model as a ranking tool and choose a threshold based on acceptable false positives.

9. Calibration Check Purpose: assess probability calibration for the high-risk class.

In [10]:
# Purpose: This notebook compares model performance, interprets the final model, and generates the primary diagnostic outputs used in the report. | code block 10.
model = trained[best_recall2_name]
class_index = list(model.classes_).index(2)
prob_pos = probas[best_recall2_name][:, class_index]

frac_pos, mean_pred = calibration_curve(y_test_bin, prob_pos, n_bins=10)

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
plt.plot(mean_pred, frac_pos, marker="o", label="Model")
plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], linestyle="--", color="gray", label="Perfectly calibrated")
plt.xlabel("Mean predicted probability")
plt.ylabel("Fraction of positives")
plt.title(f"Calibration Curve: {best_recall2_name}")
plt.legend()
plt.show()

Interpretation: Calibration¶

  • The curve below the diagonal indicates overestimation of risk probabilities.
  • Treat probabilities as relative risk scores unless calibration is applied.

Interpretation of Model Results¶

Study Objective¶

The goal is to evaluate whether models trained on MEPS longitudinal survey data behave in a logical and interpretable way for predicting future inpatient utilization risk among non-cancer adults. The emphasis is risk stratification rather than chasing marginal accuracy gains.

Outcome Distribution Context¶

The target is highly imbalanced: 92.6% have no inpatient admissions in Year 2, 5.9% have one, and 1.5% have two or more. This motivates metrics beyond overall accuracy, especially macro-F1, balanced accuracy, and class 2 recall/PR-AUC.

Overall Model Performance¶

HistGradientBoosting achieved the strongest macro-F1 in this run, with Gradient Boosting close behind. Gradient Boosting delivered the highest recall for class 2 (2+ admissions), which is valuable for high-risk targeting. Random Forest produced high overall accuracy but much lower balanced accuracy and weaker recall for minority classes, suggesting majority-class bias.

Risk Stratification Trade-offs¶

If the priority is balanced performance across all classes, HistGradientBoosting is the strongest choice. If the priority is capturing more 2+ admissions, Gradient Boosting is preferable.

Probability Quality¶

PR-AUC values are low (~0.074?0.086), which is expected given the rarity of class 2 events. The calibration curve suggests overconfident probabilities for the high-risk class, so predicted probabilities should be interpreted as ranking scores rather than exact risk unless additional calibration is applied.

Training Stability¶

For this weekly checkpoint, results should be treated as preliminary and interpreted as comparative signals rather than definitive performance.

Next Steps¶

  • Refine decision thresholds for class 2 targeting and consider probability calibration.
  • Integrate insights into the Streamlit dashboard for stakeholder review.

In [14]:
# Purpose: This notebook compares model performance, interprets the final model, and generates the primary diagnostic outputs used in the report. | code block 15.
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, average_precision_score

sample_weight_hc = compute_sample_weight(class_weight="balanced", y=y_train_hc)

models_hc = {
    "Gradient Boosting": GradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
    "HistGradientBoosting": HistGradientBoostingClassifier(
        random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
        max_depth=6,
    ),
}

trained_hc = {}
for name, model in models_hc.items():
    model.fit(X_train_hc_imp, y_train_hc, sample_weight=sample_weight_hc)
    trained_hc[name] = model

results_hc = []
for name, model in trained_hc.items():
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test_hc_imp)
    y_proba = model.predict_proba(X_test_hc_imp)[:, 1]

    results_hc.append({
        "Model": name,
        "Accuracy": accuracy_score(y_test_hc, y_pred),
        "Balanced_Accuracy": balanced_accuracy_score(y_test_hc, y_pred),
        "F1": f1_score(y_test_hc, y_pred),
        "Recall": classification_report(y_test_hc, y_pred, output_dict=True)["1"]["recall"],
        "ROC_AUC": roc_auc_score(y_test_hc, y_proba),
        "PR_AUC": average_precision_score(y_test_hc, y_proba),
    })

comparison_hc = pd.DataFrame(results_hc).sort_values("PR_AUC", ascending=False)
comparison_hc

Interpretation: High-Cost Confusion Matrix¶

  • True high-cost found: the lower-right cell. These are the correct high-cost flags.
  • High-cost missed: the lower-left cell. These are high-cost individuals the model did not catch.
  • False alarms: the upper-right cell. These are non?high-cost individuals flagged as high-cost.
  • This model is conservative: it produces few false alarms but misses many high-cost cases.
  • Diagonal cells are correct predictions; off-diagonal cells are errors.
  • This view helps decide whether the model is better used for broad screening or narrower targeting.

Analysis Notebook¶

notebooks/6.0_next_week_modeling_catboost_panel_calibration.ipynb

Purpose: CatBoost panel split, calibration review, and lift analysis.

Reviewer Guide¶

This notebook focuses on CatBoost panel validation, calibration behavior, and lift analysis for the rare 2+ admissions class.

6.0 Modeling: CatBoost + Panel Split + Calibration + Lift¶

Purpose: Extend the analysis with a stronger generalization test (panel-based split), add CatBoost, and produce decision-ready metrics (calibration + lift/deciles).

Project Context¶

Scope: Build interpretable ML models on MEPS longitudinal data (adult, non-cancer) to predict future inpatient risk and exploratory high-cost risk.

Data: MEPS Panels 23-27 (2018-2023) using longitudinal, condition, and event files (ER/IP/Rx) plus appendix link files for data integration. Outcomes use Year-2 measures; predictors use Year-1 only.

Preprocessing: Parse fixed-width .dat/.ssp files, standardize missing codes, merge on DUPERSID + PANEL, construct Year-1 utilization and condition features, drop all Year-2 predictors to prevent leakage, and create model-ready parquet outputs.

Analysis: Train and evaluate CatBoost with panel-based validation (train Panels 23-26, test Panel 27). Report Macro-F1, PR-AUC for class 2+, calibration curve, and top-decile lift.

# Purpose: Create target (inpatient risk: 0/1/2+)
TARGET_RAW = 'IPDISY2'

# Treat negative survey codes as missing for the target
NEG_CODES = [-1, -7, -8, -9]
df[TARGET_RAW] = df[TARGET_RAW].replace(NEG_CODES, np.nan)

def make_ipdisy2_class(x):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return np.nan
    if x == 0:
        return 0
    if x == 1:
        return 1
    if x >= 2:
        return 2
    return np.nan

df['Y_IPDISY2_CLASS'] = df[TARGET_RAW].apply(make_ipdisy2_class)

# Purpose: Identify categorical columns for CatBoost
import pandas as pd

X_train = X_train.copy()
X_test = X_test.copy()

cat_cols = []
for c in X_train.columns:
    if X_train[c].dtype == 'object':
        cat_cols.append(c)
    elif pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(X_train[c]) and X_train[c].nunique() <= 50:
        cat_cols.append(c)

# Cast categorical columns to string dtype to avoid pandas warnings
dtype_map = {c: 'string' for c in cat_cols}
X_train = X_train.astype(dtype_map)
X_test = X_test.astype(dtype_map)

X_train[cat_cols] = X_train[cat_cols].fillna('NA')
X_test[cat_cols] = X_test[cat_cols].fillna('NA')

cat_feature_indices = [X_train.columns.get_loc(c) for c in cat_cols]
print('Categorical features:', len(cat_cols))

# Purpose: Train CatBoost with class weights
# If catboost is not installed: pip install catboost
from catboost import CatBoostClassifier

# Compute inverse-frequency class weights
class_counts = y_train.value_counts().sort_index()
class_weights = (class_counts.sum() / class_counts).values.tolist()
print('Class weights:', class_weights)

cat_model = CatBoostClassifier(
    loss_function='MultiClass',
    eval_metric='TotalF1',
    iterations=300,
    depth=6,
    learning_rate=0.1,
    random_seed=RANDOM_STATE,
    verbose=False,
    class_weights=class_weights
)

cat_model.fit(X_train, y_train, cat_features=cat_feature_indices)
print('CatBoost trained.')

y_proba = cat_model.predict_proba(X_test)

print('Accuracy:', round(accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred), 3))
print('Balanced Acc:', round(balanced_accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred), 3))
print('Macro-F1:', round(f1_score(y_test, y_pred, average='macro'), 3))

report = classification_report(y_test, y_pred, output_dict=True, zero_division=0)
print('Recall class 2:', round(report['2']['recall'], 3))

# PR-AUC for class 2 (2+ admissions)
y_test_bin = (y_test == 2).astype(int)
precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_test_bin, y_proba[:, 2])
pr_auc = auc(recall, precision)
print('PR-AUC class 2:', round(pr_auc, 3))

# Purpose: Lift / decile analysis for class 2
# Rank by predicted probability for class 2
score_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'y_true': y_test_bin,
    'score': y_proba[:, 2]
})

score_df['decile'] = pd.qcut(score_df['score'], 10, labels=False, duplicates='drop')

lift_table = (score_df.groupby('decile')
              .agg(n=('y_true','size'),
                   positives=('y_true','sum'))
              .reset_index())

lift_table['rate'] = lift_table['positives'] / lift_table['n']
base_rate = score_df['y_true'].mean()
lift_table['lift'] = (lift_table['rate'] / base_rate)

lift_table = lift_table.sort_values('decile', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

print('Base rate (class 2):', round(base_rate, 4))
print('Top decile rate:', round(lift_table.loc[0, 'rate'], 4))
print('Top decile lift:', round(lift_table.loc[0, 'lift'], 2))

Interpretation Notes¶

  • Panel-based validation (train 23-26, test 27) provides a stronger generalization check than random splits.
  • CatBoost is well-suited for mixed numeric/categorical data and often performs well on imbalanced classes.
  • Calibration helps interpret predicted probabilities for real-world decision thresholds.
  • Lift/decile analysis shows how much better the top-risk group is compared to random selection.

Interpretation (CatBoost Panel Split)¶

  • Generalization: Using panel-based validation (train 23?26, test 27) provides a stricter, year-forward test than random splits.
  • Model balance: Macro-F1 and balanced accuracy indicate the model is not dominated by the majority class.
  • High-risk recall: Recall for class 2+ reflects how many high-risk patients are captured.
  • Ranking quality: PR-AUC for class 2 should be compared to the base rate; values well above the base rate indicate useful ranking.
  • Lift: Top-decile lift shows how much better the top 10% predicted group is compared to random selection.

SMOTENC + CatBoost (Exploratory)¶

This section tests imbalance-aware resampling using SMOTENC (training only) with a CatBoost multiclass model.

In [15]:
# Purpose: Prepare train/test matrices for SMOTENC (train only)
X_train_sm = X.loc[train_idx].copy()
X_test_sm = X.loc[test_idx].copy()
y_train_sm = y.loc[train_idx].copy()
y_test_sm = y.loc[test_idx].copy()

cost_count_cols = [c for c in X_train_sm.columns if c.endswith('_cost_y1') or c.endswith('_count_y1')]
numeric_force = set(cost_count_cols + ['AGE_MAX','TOTEXPY1','RXEXPY1','IPDISY1'])
cat_cols_sm = []
for c in X_train_sm.columns:
    if c in numeric_force:
        continue
    if X_train_sm[c].dtype == 'object':
        cat_cols_sm.append(c)
    elif pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(X_train_sm[c]) and X_train_sm[c].nunique(dropna=True) <= 50:
        cat_cols_sm.append(c)
    elif pd.api.types.is_float_dtype(X_train_sm[c]):
        vals = X_train_sm[c].dropna()
        if len(vals) > 0 and (vals % 1 == 0).all() and vals.nunique() <= 50:
            cat_cols_sm.append(c)

num_cols_sm = [c for c in X_train_sm.columns if c not in cat_cols_sm]

from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
num_imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy='median')
X_train_sm[num_cols_sm] = num_imputer.fit_transform(X_train_sm[num_cols_sm])
X_test_sm[num_cols_sm] = num_imputer.transform(X_test_sm[num_cols_sm])

X_train_sm[cat_cols_sm] = X_train_sm[cat_cols_sm].fillna(-1).astype(int)
X_test_sm[cat_cols_sm] = X_test_sm[cat_cols_sm].fillna(-1).astype(int)

cat_idx_sm = [X_train_sm.columns.get_loc(c) for c in cat_cols_sm]
print('SMOTENC categorical features:', len(cat_cols_sm))

# Purpose: Train CatBoost on SMOTENC-resampled data
from catboost import CatBoostClassifier

class_counts = pd.Series(y_train_res).value_counts().sort_index()
class_weights_sm = (class_counts.sum() / class_counts).values.tolist()

cat_model_sm = CatBoostClassifier(
    loss_function='MultiClass',
    eval_metric='TotalF1',
    iterations=300,
    depth=6,
    learning_rate=0.1,
    random_seed=RANDOM_STATE,
    verbose=False,
    class_weights=class_weights_sm
)
cat_model_sm.fit(X_train_res, y_train_res, cat_features=cat_idx_sm)
print('CatBoost (SMOTENC) trained.')
